 Looking for things to do this weekend in Singapore? Indulge in the spread of events and experiences we’ve curated for you.
 Photo: Courtesy of Arts House Group By  Harper's BAZAAR Singapore  -  published 13 Nov 2026 
 Our island may be small, but there’s always plenty to look forward to. Shut your laptop for the weekend and see our roundup of the most exciting events happening now, from pop-up markets featuring viral lifestyle brands and buzzy collaborations to must-see exhibitions and food festivals.
 Stay tuned to our curation of things to do this weekend, updated weekly.

 The Christmas Atelier
 Christmas comes early at The Christmas Atelier , which returns for its eighth edition at a new home in the Marina Bay Sands Convention Centre. This year’s theme is Delivering Christmas Magic; and with more than 130 founder-led brands selling fashion, beauty, home goods and gourmet treats; it certainly is set to deliver.
 Hosting some of the most famous homegrown brands, like Hello Arigato , known for delectable Japanese sandos and handcrafted coffee and matcha; Studio Gypsied with modern, slow-made batik apparel, it’s an event not to miss. Here are some highlights to look forward to at this iteration of The Christmas Atelier:
 Bynd Artisan: The Singapore stationery and leather goods label is a safe bet for the person on your list who loves a beautiful notebook or desk accessory.
 Ingu Skin: If you’re after skincare that’s backed by science, INGU Skin’s formulas are worth browsing.
 Tow Tow: Get your leather goods customised on the spot, which is handy for gifts that feel a little more personal.
 Kobashi: Grab a box of sourdo’nuts from this bakery, because a market run is better with a sweet treat in hand.
 This is a great place to start on your gift list and give yourself a little Christmas treat. It runs only until Saturday, so plan your visit early and book your tickets.
 The Christmas Atelier is running from now until 14 November 2026 at Hall C, level 1, Marina Bay Sands Convention Centre, 10 Bayfront Avenue, from 11am to 9pm on Friday and Saturday. For more information, visit The Christmas Atelier’s page . 
 Singapore Writers Festival
 ICYMI: Singapore Writers Festival is returning for its 2026 edition next week, and there’s plenty to look forward to. Themed around crime and mystery, you can expect a special lineup of panels that give insight into how crime writers craft an immersive world and how criminals think. Beyond that, programmes offering a literature-led trek around different parts of our island, dialogues where you can meet local writers and other interactive activties that engage various senses are also on.
 For now, purchase your Festival Pass and tickets to make sure you have access to your preferred programmes, and read our complete guide to this year’s Singapore Writers Festival for more details and a little more inspiration.
 Singapore Writers Festival runs from 13 to 22 November 2026 at various locations and timings. For more details, visit Singapore Writers Festival’s site . 
 Streetwearehouse
 Thrifters, lock in: Streetwearehouse is back for its third edition, and Weare is promising its biggest and boldest one yet. Expect racks of secondhand streetwear to dig through, plus live music and a special photobooth. You’ll find everything from Ralph Lauren tops, jorts and casual tees to highly sought-after Vietnamese brands like Hades and Devotus . If you’ve been dying to give your wardrobe a renewal, this is your opportunity.
 The first run has already passed, so this weekend is your last chance to snag anything that you’ve been eyeing. Friends, family and even pets are welcome, so it doubles as an easy weekend hangout.
 Streetwearehouse 3 is running on 14 and 15 November 2026 at #06-101, Midview City, 24 Sin Ming Lane, from 12pm to 8pm. For more information, visit weare’s page . 
 teamLab: Infinite Existence
 teamLab,  Lotus Elephant  © teamLab
 Photo: Courtesy of Ikkan Art LLC International art collective teamLab is in town for its first solo exhibit at Supper House . The showcase will see eight monitor-based works inspired by the visual language of premodern East Asian paintings, which combines multiple viewpoints, shifting perspectives and time periods into a single image.
 Here, teamLab expands on their concept of “Ultrasubjective Space”, which subverts the Western practice of featuring a single, fixed subject in their art. This exhibition in particular offers viewers and quieter and more contemplative look at teamLab’s work.
 You’ll see digital installations including “Continuous Life and Death at the Now of Eternity II”, which explores the cycle of life and death through flowers that emerge, change and disappear as the day progresses; and “Universe of Water Particles – Gold”, a virtual waterfall of cascading water particles, among others.
 teamLab: Infinite Existence runs from now to 15 November 2026 at #04-02, Supper House, Tanjong Pagar Distripark, 37 Keppel Road, from 12 to 7pm Thursdays to Saturdays and 12 to 5pm on Sundays. For more information, visit Supper House’s site. 
 Boutiques Singapore: The Gifting Edition 2026
 The Boutiques fair may only be happening later this month, but this is your PSA to get your passes soon—tickets are already flying off the shelves with a number of ticket types sold out.
 Beyond fun hands-on experiences by the likes of GOFY (who are taking over room 3A with activities like festive ornament making and live drawing), the 300 brands at this edition will see familiar names as well as 90 new ones, and there are over 200 exclusive launches to look forward to.
 Here’s where you’ll find us looking for our next best find.
 Aeter : This Taiwanese brand, new to Boutiques Singapore, offers sleek and functional totes and shoulder bags with a futuristic edge.
 Bahagia : If your BFF is a wellness girlie, she’d love Bahagia ’s selection of teas, spreads, body scrubs and roll-ons crafted by artisans all over rural parts of Asia.
 Plook Plook : Plook Plook needs no introduction. The design studio will be bringing its bestsellers—think asparagus-shaped incense holders, heirloom tomato bag charms and nesting vases—to the fair for the first time.
 Scents of P.L.T.O : For fragrances that smell as good as they look, shop this Indonesian brand. Housed in unique glass and metal bottles are scents inspired by bougie powder rooms, ancient forests, soft cashmere blankets and more.
 Romi Palais : If you’re partial to wardrobe staples like tank tops, floaty silk skirts and trousers that’ll carry you from day to night, Romi Palais is where it’s at.
 Kafe Utu : Head to Kafe Utu for a mid afternoon pick-me-up. The beloved African restaurant in the Outram area will be bringing you exclusive drinks and freshly roasted coffee beans to take home.
 Boutiques Singapore is running from 20 to 22 November 2026 at F1 Pit Building, 1 Republic Boulevard, from 11am to 9pm Friday and Saturday and 10am to 6pm on Sunday. For more information, visit Boutiques Singapore’s site. 
 “Exceptional/Everyday: New Acquisitions, New Perspectives”
 Photo: Courtesy of Peranakan Museum Most of us grew up hearing about Peranakan culture and indulging in its aromatic food on occasion, but what exactly makes an object Peranakan? Peranakan Museum ’s latest exhibition explores this question through more than 150 objects, not to identify and arrive at one answer, but rather to offer a look at the different facets of the culture and how it’s represented through a variety of objects created, passed down and bought by people.
 See a collection of items like clothing, jewellery, furniture, porcelain and more that vary from mass-produced to bespoke, with the exhibition opening with a coral-red kamcheng (jar with a covered lid)—the first known Peranakan object to join the National Collection in 1963.
 “Exceptional/Everyday: New Acquisitions, New Perspectives” runs from now to 27 August 2027 at the Special Exhibitions Gallery of the Peranakan Museum, 39 Armenian Street, from 10am to 6.30pm Sundays to Thursdays and 10am to 8.30pm on Fridays. For more information, visit Peranakan Museum’s site . 
 “Sacred Caves: Dunhuang, Buddhism and the Silk Road”
 Photo: Courtesy of Dunhuang Academy ICYMI, there’s a new exhibition at the Asian Civilisations Museum that everyone’s been talking about. Titled “Sacred Caves: Dunhuang, Buddhism and the Silk Road”, the showcase revisits the storied history of Dunhuang, a city in northwest China connected to India and the Middle East that played a vital role in trade, religion and cultural exchanges in ancient times. 
 For this exhibition, the first of its kind in Southeast Asia, ACM collaborated with Dunhuang Academy to bring life-sized replicas and original artwork from the Mogao Caves. See how life was really like more than a thousand years ago with sculptures and paintings from the Tang and Sui dynasties without needing to travel to the edge of the Gobi desert.
 “Sacred Caves: Dunhuang, Buddhism and the Silk Road” runs from now to 7 March 2027 at Asian Civilisations Museum, 1 Empress Place, from 10am to 7pm Sundays to Thursdays and 10am to 9pm on Fridays. For more information, visit ACM’s site.

 The Story of Studio Ghibli
 Photo: Courtesy of Studio Ghibli Further out on the horizon, but worth flagging now, is the world premiere of The Story of Studio Ghibli at Gardens by the Bay this December. Spanning nearly 3,500 square metres, it will be the first time an exhibition of this scale dedicated to the storied Japanese animation studio has opened anywhere in the world, with Singapore given the honour of hosting its debut.
 The show promises 12 fully realised environments, each drawing from a different corner of the Ghibli universe. From the pastoral wonder of My Neighbor Totoro to the eerie, bathhouse-bound world of Spirited Away , the coming-of-age charm of Kiki's Delivery Service , and the environmental gravity of Princess Mononoke .
 For a studio whose visual language has become genuinely iconic, and instantly recognisable even to those who've never seen the films, the promise of walking through these worlds physically, rather than watching them on screen, is a significant one.
 The Story Of Studio Ghibli runs from 18 December 2026 to 4 July 2027 at West Lawn, Gardens by the Bay, 18 Marina Drive. Book an early bird ticket on Klook here .

 “Singapore Odyssea: A Journey Through Time”
 Photo: Courtesy of National Museum of Singapore “Singapore Odyssea: A Journey Through Time”, a permanent exhibition staged at National Museum of Singapore, encourages visitors to voyage into Singapore’s 700 years of history, hinging on the sea as a key player to our island’s transformation over the years.
 The showcase happens over five chapters, opening with a ‘time-travelling’ vessel that offers a glimpse of Singapore in the future, before taking guests back in time to see pivotal points in Singapore’s history. Descend the ramp and see moments from Singapore’s first National Day Parade, early nation-building efforts and our mythical past along the way, all told from the perspective of the sea.
 More magic awaits at the base of the Glass Rotunda. Step through a towering digital waterfall to find more scenes from the past, and tap your RFID bracelet against a ‘well’ to release your adopted magical companion into the ocean.
 “Singapore Odyssea: A Journey Through Time” runs daily from 10am to 6pm. Book a slot here and find more information on National Museum of Singapore’s website .

 Singapore Stories: ​Pathways and Detours in Art
 Photo: Courtesy of National Gallery Singapore “Singapore Stories: Pathways and Detours in Art” is a long-term exhibition at `National Gallery Singapore. The first part explores Singapore’s stories and societal changes through art from the 19th century to the 1960s. Featuring over 200 artworks and artefacts across four sections, the exhibition showcases how artists such as Georgette Chen , Liu Kang , Annaratnam Gunaratnam , P. Ramlee , have experimented with medium and expression while addressing themes like colonialism, urban change, and globalisation.
